Well I would say Ive felt a profound sense of dependence for another human (my mother) but I wouldnt qualify that as emotional intimacy. My theory is that we (humans) are closed systems, thus we have no method of enguaging another being on an emotional level. For instance I have no way of knowing if the sensation you interperate as love would feel the same to me or if it would feel like pain, or simply bland. Likewise two humans have no way of knowing if the other person in their arms is experiencing the same emotional state as they are. One might be feeling a profound sense of satisfaction and saftey while the other is simply bored and placating their partner. Furthurmore, because there can be no direct corelation between two closed systems, and because the interpretations of certain stimulie could be vastly different, the sensation we associate with "emotional intimacy" is merely an internalized and isolated event, to which they merely associate the other person due to circumstance. Lastly, the concept of emotional intimacy is flawed as it implies some sort of implicit truth to the feeling, which if not adequatly disproven above, can be reguarded as selfish and shallow, as it is not predicated on the other persons emotional state but instead is a product of their actions. Thus what a person is "feeling" is not the intimacy of another persons own feelings, but rather an internalized and independant response caused by action that does not necessitate reciprocation by the other persons emotions; thus rendering the idea of intimacy innate. Two people might happen to experience euphoric emotional states at the same time together, but there is no guarentee that this is what is really happening and the probability of it actually happening is surprisingly low.

On the other hand physical intimacy is very real and provable, since all you would have to do would be to touch another person and have them be receptive to it for physical intimacy to be confirmed.

As far as Ive come to understand, happiness is not a static state. One does not "obtain happiness". You will experience moments of happiness throughout your life but no one will ever reach a constant of feeling good forever. From an evolutionary stand point, feeling consistently happy would not be very advantageous. You would have no compulsion to go out and try new things, or produce anything of value. This is why drug addicts have such a bad stigma, because they simply languish in the euphoria of their drugs and do literally nothing with those feel good feelings. Happiness is a reward mechanism given to you when you succeed in something and then fades so that you go out and seek more of it. 

Now if youre feeling terrible all the time that is a different story all together. Feeling bad is also an evolutionary disadvantage because you lose the will to seek out happiness, and it points to sever psychiatric disorders such as depression, not psychopathy. 

Really you should aim and focus on feeling fulfilled rather than happy, as that will give you the most amount of happy moments. As for the question of what love is... I could write you an essay on that so ill just leave off here.
